messages:
Jun Park: Quick sync — I ran a fresh set of perf runs for the FlashAttention variants w/ fused RoPE and ALiBi fallback. Seeing a regression for long seqs when we hit paged-attn + KV cache eviction. Notes below.

Priya Nair: Can you paste the minimal repro? which binary/commit?

Jun Park: commit d9f3a2e (kernel-selection-refactor). Bench command: `./bench/attn_bench --model gpt-3-small --seq 8192 --bs 1 --kernel flash_fused_rope --paged true --kv-cache on`

Mateo Rivera: Interesting — on my rig the flash_fused_rope path is ~1.8x faster for seq<=2048, but above ~4k we start seeing host-GPU copies due to paged-attn working set thrash. Was the kernel selector preferring flash even when memory would cause paging?

Jun Park: Exactly. Kernel selector currently prioritizes peak-throughput kernels from perf table without factoring in active KV cache pages. So it picks flash_fused_rope, kernel blows memory working set past TLB/PCI window and we incur micro-bursts of page faults.

Alex Chen: Do we log the chosen kernel per-request anywhere? I remember we had a lightweight metric but it was disabled.

Lisa Gomez: infra-bot: reported deploy d9f3a2e to staging at 2025-10-12T07:12:00Z :rocket:

infra-bot: perf-alert: 2025-10-12T07:15:30Z - spike in P99 for /generate using model=gpt-3-small seq=8192

Priya Nair: Proposal: extend kernel selector heuristic with a working-set estimator. Inputs: seq_len, kv_cache_size, active_paged_pages, free_gpu_mem, batch_effective_tokens. If estimated working set > mem_threshold then choose paged-aware or fused-lite kernel.

Mateo Rivera: +1. Also we should add a fast runtime check for `kv_cache_active_pages()` that can be polled per-request. If >n pages, prefer kernels that do sequential block reads (lower random IO) and have lower peak memory.

Alex Chen: For documentation/telemetry let's add these fields to the trace: chosen_kernel, estimator_score, fallback_reason. That way we can correlate selector mistakes with perf regressions.

Jun Park: I ran nvprof and cupy timers — attached short excerpt:
```
# nvprof snippet
kernel: flash_fused_rope  time: 1.92ms  alloc_peak: 4.2GB  page_faults: 12
kernel: flash_basic       time: 2.85ms  alloc_peak: 2.1GB  page_faults: 0
```
So flash is faster but causes page faults that add jitter and increase p99.

Lisa Gomez: Any quick mitigation we can ship? A conservative fix would be: if seq>4096 && kv_cache_pages>8 then force kernel=flash_basic.

Priya Nair: That heuristic is reasonable as an interim. We'll need a test matrix: seq in {1024,2048,4096,8192}, batch {1,4}, kv_cache_pages {0,4,16} across kernels {flash_fused_rope, flash_basic, paged_attn}. I'll add to CI perf-suite.

Mateo Rivera: Also need to validate rotary dims behavior: fused RoPE assumes rotary dim equals model rotary config. There was a mismatch in an older loader (rotary_dims=64 vs 128) that forced an unoptimized fallback. Add an assertion in model-onboard to ensure rotary dim alignment or auto-pad to optimized path.

Jun Park: Good call — that mismatch could trigger the fallback path and explain a hit in some experiments.

Alex Chen: Plan: (1) Add estimator + runtime telemetry (2 days). (2) Ship conservative kernel bias rule for long seqs (1 day). (3) Add CI matrix and rotary-dim assertion (2 days). Who wants to own (1)?

Priya Nair: I'll own (1) and the telemetry work. Mateo will help with estimator math.

Mateo Rivera: I'll prototype estimator tomorrow and push a branch. Jun, can you attach the full nvprof traces and sample logs?

Jun Park: Pushed traces to /mnt/bench/traces/d9f3a2e/ and added a short HTML diff in the ticket.

Lisa Gomez: Adding to eng-ml sprint board. Tagging @ops for a staging run after the conservative rule is live. :white_check_mark:

Jun Park: Thanks team — let's reconvene after the CI matrix lands.

Alex Chen: LGTM :thumbsup:
